Confirmed real structural differences from the template by reading the retained assembly directly, not by assuming the template's body: this owner takes no argument (r0 is clobbered before ever being read, so work's 0x7828 state pointer must already be established by a prior call); it registers only one draw routine (heap kind 46, no kind 47) and only one periodic callback (0x080CD261, no 0x080DBB9D) and tears down only that one pair at the end; it reads `facing` once before the frame loop instead of every frame; it has an entirely new 64-entry/28-byte-stride record table at work+0x7080 with no member_orbit counterpart, zeroed before the main loop; and its per-member drawing is 3 sprites indexed by member*3+i with a persistent per-slot angle accumulator (field 0xC, advanced by 0x200 every draw) plus a static i*0x5555 per-sprite offset, rather than the template's 4-sprites-recomputed-from-frame-number. Verified the two `bl Func_080072f0` / `bl Func_080072f8` sites are indirect calls through games/gs1/asm/080072e4.s's r3 and r5 call-via slots respectively (not real Func_080072fN symbols): the r3 site is modeled with the template's own proven idiom `((WordCopyFn)0x03001388)(dest, src, words)`; the r5 site's pointer is heap_cache[7] (the kind-46 draw routine), stored in a local `rect_fn` and called as `((DrawRectangleFn)rect_fn)(...)`, since r5 is not one of the four APCS argument registers. candidate-show --align confirms the first 11 instructions (the full heap_cache/cursor/facing prologue through the mode-1 Func_080cd594 call) are byte-identical (matched_prefix=11), and every branch target and call site in the normalized diff lines up positionally with no opcode mismatches -- the entire 229-halfword residual is `!`-class operand substitutions (registers and their matching stack-spill offsets), not a missing or extra instruction shape, control-flow difference, or wrong call target. The dominant single cause is that this compiler keeps `work` in fp for the whole function where the reference keeps it in r9 (and correspondingly the member-loop `screen[2]` local, which the reference keeps in fp, is fully stack-spilled here instead of getting any high register at all); nearly every other `!`/`+`/`-` line in the diff is a direct downstream consequence (the reference's `mov r5,r9; ldr r3,[r5,r2]` register-indexed-load idiom for repeated work->0x7828 reads becomes this candidate's `ldr r3,[pc,#N]; add r3,fp; ldr r3,[r3,#0]` fresh-pool-reload idiom instead, and every stack slot after the first spill shifts by 4-8 bytes along with the smaller 80-byte vs 88-byte frame). This is the exact fp/r9 residual already documented independently on three siblings in this same family (games/gs1/recon/en/main/080d59b0.json, 080d82b0.json is its origin point, 080dc1ec.json) for the same shared 0x03001eec work-block idiom; see rejected_experiments below for this owner's own from-scratch confirmation that it is not source-shape-controllable here either.

rejected_experiments: Scoping `screen`/`screen2`/`record`/loop temporaries into their tightest enclosing block (matching the template's own nested-declaration style) instead of declaring everything at function top level: byte-for-byte identical candidate-show output (612/616/229/244) in both directions -- this compiler's register allocator is insensitive to C89 lexical declaration scope for this owner, as already found independently on sibling 080d59b0.

Reordering the top-level scalar-local declarations (moving `work` to the end of the declaration list, after canvas/palette/status/rect_fn/facing/y_offset): no change at all (612/616/229/244) -- declaration order does not affect this compiler's pseudo-register priority for this owner either.

Widening the `screen`/`screen2` member-loop buffers from 2 words to 3 (matching the template's 3-word `screen[3]`, on the theory that the reference's 8-byte-larger frame meant a missing third word): regressed to 640/616/271/260 and lost 2 bytes of matched_prefix -- these buffers are genuinely 2 words each; the frame-size gap is a downstream spill-slot symptom of the fp/r9 register choice below, not a missing local.

Introducing a named `state` local reassigned via `state = M2C_FIELD(work, void **, 0x7828);` immediately before every dereference (matching the 080d82b0.c sibling's own `target = M2C_FIELD(...)` re-assignment style, instead of nesting the field read inline at each use site): regressed slightly to 612/616/230/258 -- reverted to the inline nested form.

These four experiments independently reproduce the same conclusion 080d59b0.json and 080dc1ec.json already recorded for two other members of this family: this compiler's choice of fp over r9 for a whole-function loop-invariant work-block pointer is not controllable from declaration order, block scope, buffer sizing, or inline-vs-named field-read spelling. Per the project's standing guidance for this documented residual class, no register-hint hack or open-ended permutation search was attempted to force r9.

compiler_backend_evidence_2026_08_31: The allocator decoder identifies pseudo 34 as the source variable work: 18 uses across 175 instructions, one definition, no deaths, and 15 crossed calls. Canonical allocation maps it to r11/fp while the retained owner maps the same lifetime to r9.

With the single shipped optimization change -fno-rerun-cse-after-loop, the generated instruction stream changes mov fp,r1 to mov r9,r1 exactly as the reference does, and every subsequent palette-copy use also changes from mov r1,fp to the reference's mov r1,r9. The candidate simultaneously becomes exact-extent and equal-topology.

The remaining 208 halfwords retain the 80-byte candidate frame versus the reference's 88-byte frame and different promotion/spill choices for member-loop arrays and counters. No ABI allocation flag improves them; every -ffixed-rN and -fcall-used-rN probe for r8-r11 regresses to 291-294 halfwords and changes extent to 620 bytes.

The decoder's only structural suggestion was a member-count guard inversion. Rewriting the C as an explicit empty zero-count arm plus else compiled byte-identically, confirming GCC folds that spelling before allocation. The edit was reverted.

No other Golden Sun decompilation project, symbol map, or pseudocode dump was consulted.
This candidate claims zero DONE bytes; it is a measured-draft, not adopted.

Semantic summary: a small battle-presentation sub-effect sharing the 0x03001eec work block with 080ce85c and its siblings. Takes no argument (its state pointer must already be set up by a caller). Opens one display window (heap kind 46), copies a palette through the shared IWRAM word-copy routine, and sets a BG2-affine-related pair of work fields to (1,0) then (2,75) before registering one periodic callback (0x080CD261, 0x480-frame interval). Computes a vertical offset from state field 4 and writes it (shifted) to the BG affine Y register, then zeroes a new 64-entry/28-byte orbit-angle record table. Runs member_count*16+64 frames; each frame re-derives every listed party member's screen position via Func_080e396c (adjusted by the vertical offset) and, for the 64-frame window each member is active, also calls Func_080e3944 on that member's 3D position for its side effects only, then draws 3 sprites per member orbiting a persistent per-slot angle accumulator advanced by 0x200 per draw, spaced 120 degrees apart, through the single traced draw-routine function pointer.

Value_000000a9 follows the established Value_<hex> spelling for a small absolute link-time resource id (games/gs1/src/battle/effects/member_orbit/run.c's own Value_000000af comment documents the same reasoning: an ordinary integer literal would compile to a `movs` immediate, not the reference's literal-pool load).

Func_080e396c(s32 member_id, s32 *screen) is a distinct callee from the already-used Func_080e3944(void *source, void *screen): the retained assembly calls the two at different addresses with different argument shapes (member id directly vs. a 3-word position record), so they were declared and used as separate functions rather than assumed to be the same callee.
